A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across layout changes and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on noisy GLUE datasets, including downstream accuracy, layer comparisons, aggregation experiments, and noise-detection analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds autoregressive-dataset evaluations, voting sensitivity experiments, sample-rank analyses, and targeted Llama experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed Rank and Vote procedures, including their restriction to correctly predicted validation samples, remain unchanged in Section 3.3 and Equations 9–10. Varying voting parameters and selecting particular modules are experimental settings; the additional attribution techniques are comparators.

E1.justification: Appendix J extends evaluation beyond the retained eight noisy GLUE tasks to Grammar, Math, and Math With Reasoning instruction datasets. These evaluate whether influence rankings recover semantic-category relationships, substantially broadening coverage beyond detecting injected label noise.

E2.justification: The new comparisons in Figures 23–26 evaluate Outlier Gradient, Kronfluence/EKFAC, and RepSim alongside TracIn, Cosine, and DataInf. RepSim includes last-token and mean-token variants. This substantially broadens the evaluated attribution approaches; the original GLUE comparator sets remain intact.

E3.justification: The original GLUE protocol is retained. New protocols include semantic-category AUC and Recall evaluation in Appendix J, a voting-cutoff sweep from 10 to 100 in steps of 10 in Appendix L, and selected Llama Value B modules with k=20 in Appendix M. These are additional experimental designs, not evidence that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices K–M add substantial diagnostics: tracking benign and noisy sample ranks across layers, testing sensitivity to voting cutoff across LoRA modules, and investigating whether module selection remedies Llama's weak filtering performance. These extend the earlier layer correlations and noise-distribution analyses.

E5.justification: v2 adds an explicit Friedman test to Figure 2 and reports 95% confidence intervals over 10 seeds in Figures 27–28. The original ten-seed design and Wilcoxon reporting remain; the PDFs do not establish an increased run count for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and the original plots retain their results, while Appendices J–M add extensive findings. For example, Table 7 reports rank 6.80 ± 4.10 for Cosine/Vote on v-b-9 versus 9.40 ± 6.00 for Random, with reported Wilcoxon p=0.0072. This is a new selected-module comparison, not a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations 1–10, cancellation theorem, and Appendix G proof are substantively unchanged. The new empirical analyses introduce no new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about cancellation's unreliability, informative attention layers, Rank/Vote aggregation, and NDR-based evaluation. The added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: New discussion hypothesizes that Llama's reduced depth contributes to its weak attribution performance and interprets rank trajectories through persistent noisy outliers. Appendix L also identifies how optimal voting cutoff depends on noise level as unresolved. These refine the existing interpretations and applicability guidance.

D1.justification: Section 7 newly supplies a code-repository link, seed-script information, deterministic PyTorch settings, and server details. Appendix J documents comparator implementation choices and learning rates. These are additional disclosures; the new 40GB-per-GPU statement is inconsistent with the retained A100 80GB description in Appendix A.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning through two new discussions: responding to recent evidence of influence-function failures, especially Li et al. (2025), and connecting layer localization and aggregation to ROME, R-ROME, MEMIT, and EMMET. These introduce substantive relationships to prior research beyond additional citations.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 adds a reproducibility section, Appendices J–M, and supporting cross-references, with localized wording and heading changes. The additions do not constitute extensive rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds multi-panel AUC/Recall plots, sample-rank plots, three-dimensional voting-sensitivity displays, and Table 7. The ICLR template also changes margins, headers, sizing, and table placement throughout. Earlier figures remain present, mostly with renumbering and resizing.

improvement.justification: v1's empirical support was confined to synthetic-label-noise filtering on GLUE. Appendix J substantially strengthens the scope of validation through semantic-category attribution tasks and additional comparators, while Appendices K–M investigate voting sensitivity and the Llama failure case. These additions improve the evidence behind practical layer-selection guidance, alongside new reproducibility disclosures. Table 7's unclear task quantities and inconsistent GPU descriptions introduce reporting weaknesses, but they do not outweigh the substantial empirical gains.
